title: Days Out Discount Codes, Offers & Kids-Go-Free Deals
description: Real days out discount codes and offers: 2FOR1 with train tickets, kids-go-free deals, annual passes and free museum days in the UK, US and Europe.
h1: Days out discount codes and offers that actually work
intro: No expired codes, no click-bait. Every offer below is a real, current scheme we have checked on the official website, with the date we checked it.

image.alt: A family flying a kite in a field under a clear blue sky

blocks.title: How Scout checks a deal
blocks.text: If it isn’t on the official website, it doesn’t go on this page. Most of the best savings need no code at all, just the right ticket, card or badge.
points: Each offer shows the date we last checked it
Codes appear only when they are real and current
Offers change, so confirm the terms before you pay

items.title: 2FOR1 and money off attractions when you travel by train
items.text: Travel by train and show a valid National Rail ticket to get 2FOR1 entry or other discounts at attractions across the UK.
items.nocode: No code: voucher or booking reference
items.terms: Valid National Rail ticket needed. Oyster, contactless and TfL tickets don’t qualify. Some offers need pre-booking.

items.title: One pass for LEGOLAND, Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, Chessington, SEA LIFE and more
items.text: For 2026 there are three passes: Essential, Gold and Platinum. Discovery and Silver have been withdrawn, and Blackpool attractions aren’t included on new or renewed passes.
items.terms: You still need to pre-book visits. Exclusion dates vary by pass.

items.title: Money off theme parks, zoos, cinemas and restaurants
items.text: A paid family discount membership. Pick an offer in the app and get a code or barcode. It has offered a low-cost 30-day trial in 2026.
items.nocode: Codes are issued in the app
items.terms: Paid membership. Check renewal terms before the trial ends.

items.title: Free child entry at 200+ UK attractions
items.text: Children under 16 who earn a Blue Peter badge get free entry at participating attractions when an adult pays and they show their badge and ID card.
items.terms: Merlin attractions stopped taking badges in 2017. Badges can take weeks to arrive.

items.title: Swap Clubcard vouchers for days out
items.text: Clubcard Reward Partners have included days out such as Alton Towers Resort in 2026. Exchange rates and partners change, so check the app.
items.terms: Partners and values change. Check expiry dates on your vouchers.

items.title: Under-5s go free at most properties
items.text: Both charities let children under 5 in free at most sites, and family memberships can cover the rest of the gang for a year.
items.terms: Check each property: some events and car parks charge extra.

items.title: Book direct, and under-5s go free
items.text: Children aged 4 and under go free with a ticket. Booking on the official site avoids reseller mark-ups. Transport packages cost more.
items.terms: Advance booking only: no tickets on arrival.

items.merchant: Bank of America Museums on Us
items.title: Free museum entry on the first full weekend of every month
items.text: Bank of America, Merrill and Private Bank cardholders get one free general admission at participating museums. The next weekend is 7–8 November 2026.
items.terms: Cardholder only, no guests. Special exhibitions excluded.

items.title: Free or reduced entry with an EBT card
items.text: Families receiving SNAP benefits can show an EBT card for free or reduced admission at hundreds of participating museums across the US.
items.terms: Rules (group size, price) vary by museum.

items.title: Free national parks pass for fourth graders
items.text: US fourth graders (and home-schooled 10-year-olds) can get a free pass that covers entrance fees for the family at federal lands. The 2026–27 pass runs to 31 August 2027.
items.terms: Covers entrance fees, not camping or tours.

items.title: Official special offers and free kids’ dining deals
items.text: Disney lists current ticket and hotel offers on its official site, and some 2026 UK packages have included free dining for children aged 3–9.
items.nocode: No code: offers apply when you book
items.terms: Offers have limited dates and conditions.

items.title: Seasonal hotel and ticket offers
items.text: Disneyland Paris runs seasonal offers on its official site. Under-3s always go free.
items.nocode: No code: offers apply when you book
items.terms: Offer dates, eligible hotels and conditions vary.

items.title: Free for under-18s at national museums
items.text: France’s national museums, including the Louvre, admit under-18s free. EU/EEA residents aged 18–25 usually go free too.
items.terms: Timed booking is often still required, even for free tickets.

items.title: “Domenica al museo”: free state museums on the first Sunday of the month
items.text: Italian state museums and archaeological sites have opened for free on the first Sunday of the month. Expect crowds and check booking rules.
items.terms: Some sites need advance reservation on free days.

sections.h2: Why we don’t list hundreds of codes
sections.html: Many voucher sites fill pages with codes that expired years ago, just to rank in Google. We think that wastes your time. We list fewer offers, but each one is real. Learn how to spot a fake discount code.

sections.h2: More ways to save on days out
sections.html:
• Under-5s free: many attractions, including National Trust and English Heritage sites, let little ones in free.
  • Carers: lots of attractions offer free or discounted carer tickets for disabled visitors. Ask before booking.
  • Gift Aid tickets: charity attractions often offer a ticket with an optional donation. You can usually choose the standard price instead.
  • Annual passes: compare an annual pass against day tickets.
  • Free days: see our free days out guide.

faqs.q: Are days out discount codes real?
faqs.a: Some are, but many codes on voucher sites are expired or never worked. The most reliable savings come from official schemes like the National Rail Days Out Guide, memberships, annual passes and kids-go-free rules.

faqs.q: How does 2FOR1 with National Rail work?
faqs.a: You travel by train to the attraction, then show your valid National Rail ticket with a Days Out Guide voucher or booking reference to get the offer. Oyster, contactless and TfL tickets don’t qualify. Full guide.
Usually not. Most attractions allow one offer per ticket, so compare the offers and use the biggest saving.
